utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. Good morning, everybody. Can we hear the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. This is Case Number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And same procedure as every day, appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Nicholas Koumjian with Ruth Karper for the Prosecution, Your Honours. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Branko Lukic with Mr. Danilo Cirkovic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we start, a very brief comment, having a look on yesterday's transcript, first of all, to the Defence, please don't misunderstand the comments given by the Bench. It's just to concentrate on the real and major issues of the case, and please take it as given with the principle, jura novit curia, the Judges know the laws as applicable in this court and therefore we should take care to proceed as soon as possible. And you may draw some conclusions from the remarks of the Judges on the relevance, what the Judges themselves regard as really relevant. So please understand the comments in this spirit. And as regards you, also good morning to you, Witness, please be so kind also in the interest of the Defence, provide us with precise and clear but hopefully short answers. And this being said, we may start immediately with the cross-examination going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Doctor.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you get enough rest?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Did you?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So did I. I hope this will not prove to be my own testimony. Let's start immediately, as our time is limited. I will try not to go into any legal issues today, but rather discuss specific and concrete issues. On Monday's transcript, page 27, line 21, you say that the SDA advocated the idea that, after the 1991 elections, the left-wing parties should also be represented in organs of authority. Can you, perhaps, tell us whether there is any written evidence as to these intentions by the SDA and where this evidence may be found?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was during the negotiations between the parties. This idea was proposed by SDA leaders, and we weren't talking about left-wing parties but about opposition parties in general. As these were coordination meetings, I'm not sure there's any written trace. But at any rate, perhaps we could find a witness who could confirm this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did the coalition -- was the coalition not agreed with the SDS and the HDZ at the republican level?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was only a month after the elections. What I have talked about was immediately after the elections.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was it known before the election that the SDA, SDS, and HDZ would enter a coalition?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were there any talks to this effect for these two parties to enter a coalition?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there were never any talks about this sort of coalition.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was there a coalition between the SDA and the HDZ against the SDS? In Bosnia and Herzegovina and after the establishment of power in Bosnia and Herzegovina, on the basis of the 1991 elections, of course?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 1991 elections? You are probably referring to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The first democratic elections.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in November 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise, November 1990.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was never, not at any single moment, such a coalition of the SDA and the HDZ against the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 1992 -- 1991 and 1992 is the period we're talking about. Were there any meetings organised by the SDA and the HDZ at which such a coalition was advocated, the idea of a coalition against the SDS? And were any flags displayed at these meetings, at these rallies, of the SDA and the HDZ? I would like to add the following: Not only whether the flags were displayed, but whether they were actually tied up one after the other.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure that at no meeting of the SDA was anything ever said against any of the peoples or any of the parties. And I'm also sure that no coalition of the SDA and the HDZ was ever referred to in terms of a coalition against the SDS. It is true that flags were tied up individually. Sometimes even as many as a hundred thousand people attended these meetings, but that in itself proves and means nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to briefly go back to the event in Hambarine on the 22nd of May, 1992. Was the car that was fired at, at the checkpoint in Hambarine, coming from the direction of Ljubija?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You claim that you heard that passengers, from the car that was fired at, were requested to turn in their weapons?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why were they not asked to turn in their weapons on their way into Hambarine but rather on the way out as they were leaving for Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The witness can't answer this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said before that you examined the wounded and found that two of them were dead. Did you move them from the spot, or did they always remain in the exact place where they were wounded?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found them. They were lying maybe several metres away from the car, and I only examined them, but I didn't move them from that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did anyone else move their bodies? Do you know that? Are you familiar with that information?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know if they were ever left in that place, unattended by the persons manning the checkpoint? Were they simply left there? Were people manning the checkpoint going somewhere else and leaving them behind?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to remind you that an armoured vehicle arrived at the scene which left after a brief debate that I had described yesterday, then fired at the checkpoint with light artillery weapons. So no one could stay in that place, because that place was under fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's precisely the point. That's why I'm asking you, because of the fact that fire was opened at the checkpoint. Were these wounded people left there? Were they carried off? Because obviously, there was no one there when the place came under fire, or did, perhaps, the armoured vehicle fire anyway even if the wounded were still there?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the latter is true. The armoured vehicle firing paid no attention whatsoever to the fact that there were wounded people lying on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But as there was no one at the checkpoint, as you have said, can we draw the conclusion that these wounded people were just simply left to their own devices where they were?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were abandoned by people who were in a position to take them to a hospital, the people from the armoured vehicle. I asked them to take these wounded to a hospital because we couldn't. So they were the ones who actually left them behind, not we.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As I have not received an answer, I must ask you the following: Does this mean that one of the persons from the checkpoint stood beside Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. them or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Objection. That's vague as to the time we're talking about. The witness described a series of events. Some took place before he arrived, undoubtedly some took place after he left. During the time he was there, it was before the armoured car came, when the armoured car came. The question is not precise as to the time he's asking when the people from the checkpoint stood beside the wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The period we're discussing the whole time is the moment the armoured vehicle fired at the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already answered that question. At that moment, there was no one beside the wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I just ask --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: -- To remind the witness to pause before answering. I know the interpreters have a little trouble keeping up, and I don't have a chance to hear the question before he answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This is true for all the witnesses. Please try not to overlap. And for the witness, please don't, also in your own interest, be too fast with the answer. First rethink, for example, in this case, which is the accurate period of time, and then answer later, that we have really precise answers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you know today who fired at the checkpoint in Hambarine, in terms of the events that we have just been talking about?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you name any names, if we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We don't have to. I can say it publicly. First, one of the four persons from the car fired at the persons manning the checkpoint, who then threw themselves on the ground. And then a young man whose last name I remember, Habibovic, who was not a member of the unit manning the checkpoint, but he happened to be there, so he fired, too. I can mention his name because he was later killed in the Omarska camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there any investigation into these murders?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked for an investigation to be carried out, but as far as I know, it never was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us how you convened the meetings that were held in Hambarine? You say that you had no phone available at that time.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By courier, persons who physically went from one place to another on the ground and notified other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were they free to move around, as Mr. Cehajic was?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of those persons who were not, in a manner of speaking, prominent could move about freely, up to a certain point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In order to convene these meetings, did you use the radio connection that was set up in Hambarine?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the exact number of people organised and drafted into the Territorial Defence forces in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Your Honour, we have one exhibit received from the OTP, but we have never received the translation of this document. So if you agree, we would like to ask this witness to read this information, and I hope that the Prosecution can provide us with the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think it's appropriate, and let's decide on the formal translation when we have seen the probative value of this document and when it's done in the transcript, we have already the English and the French version. But as I understood correctly it's not yet tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's not yet tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then it will be tendered by the Defence. And the new Document Number will be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be D6, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: D6, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask counsel for the record to identify the ERN number stamped on the document, and just for the Trial Chamber's information, not all documents we have have ever been submitted for translation. If the Trial Chamber decides it should be translated, we could submit it to CLSS or the Defence could submit it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No, it's quite clear we should proceed in the way we did it in the past to ask a witness to read such a document out, and then we decide later whether or not we need an additional formal translation. So please proceed. Do you have any 65 ter number? This would be really helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But it's not from the last complete documents, last pile of documents. I marked it as B581.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just so the record is clear --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll give the document to the Prosecution so they can follow because even this ERN number is not easily readable, so I cannot...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mujadzic, you heard what our problem was about. We have no translation, so the way this Trial Chamber proceeds is for the document to be read so that both the Judges who speak English and the Judge who speaks French may get a proper translation of this document. Would you be so kind as to read out the whole document from top to bottom.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By all means.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can it be put on the ELMO for the benefit of the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: For the benefit of the interpreters and the Judges, please, could one copy be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Your Honour, I have enough documents for the translators and for the Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just to clarify for the record, this was not an exhibit, and the number that counsel gave is apparently a disclosure number. It was not on the 65 ter exhibit list. It's a disclosure number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Disclosure number, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And not all items disclosed are translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: As I can see through the dark glasses, the booths are prepared, then we can start. Witness, would you be so kind and start reading everything you can identify on this document, to put it this way.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Top right corner of the document, handwritten number, 11212/413. Date the 11th of May, 1992. Upper left corner: "MUP of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, number 1070," and below, the 29th of April, 1992. Then, the remark: "Very urgent." Below, CSB, Security Services Centre, to all, and addressed to the head. Below, public security station, to all, the head. And below, the secretariat of the interior affairs, Sarajevo, to the secretary. "It is necessary that all Security Services Centres, public security stations, and the Sarajevo SUP take all the necessary measures and actions within their competence to ensure the implementation of orders by the commander of the Territorial Defence staff of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Number 02/1451, dated 29th of April, 1992, which we forward to you in the original. Order on the implementation of the decision of the presidency of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, number 02-11-327/92. Pursuant to a decision of the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, number 02-11-327/92, dated the 27th of April, 1992, on the withdrawal of JNA units from the territory of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and due to failure to observe with this decision by the presidency and the incipient plunder and Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. robbery of property of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina by the former JNA, I hereby order, one, carry out, set up blockades on all roads in the territory of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina where units of the former JNA are beginning to evacuate technical and materiel equipment in immediate coordination with the MUP forces." Page 2: "Blockade the wider region of military facilities from which there have been attempts to evacuate materiel equipment, set up blockades with various formation and unnatural obstacles to be manned by units of the Territorial Defence of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the MUP. Use unannounced convoys -- unannounced convoys of the units of the former JNA and without the MUP's escort, prevent anyone from leaving the barracks and communicating in the territory of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Quickly plan and initiate combat operations in the entire territory of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and coordinate them with the Territorial Defence staff of the region, the district, and the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. "When planning combat operations, plan also comprehensive measures to protect the population and the material goods owned by the citizens of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Minister of the interior, Alija Delimustafic." End of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Dr. Mujadzic, is this document dated 29th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two dates on this document. One is typewritten, the 29th of April, 1992. And the other is handwritten and is the 11th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know when the military columns in Tuzla and the one in Dobravojacka Street in Sarajevo came under attack?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know the exact dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of these attacks?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that I would describe them as attacks. Those were conflicts, and I did hear about them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you hear of any negotiations and any promises made to these convoys, that they would be granted free passage both in Tuzla and in Dobravojacka Street in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I'm not familiar with these details.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the time the document that you have just read out was issued, do you know whether the representatives of the Serbian people were also members of this presidency, whether they were still on the presidency in question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, if this is the document that I believe the witness referred to in direct examination, his testimony is that it was never issued. So the question assumes a fact that the witness has denied in his examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Probably the Defence could put the question into another form.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During your examination-in-chief, as my learned colleague has just reminded me, you stated that this document was never issued. Did you base your statement on the fact that the presidency itself denied having ever issued such a document, or is it the case that you have some additional knowledge about this issue?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of a public communique of the presidency, the issuing of this document was denied.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 29th of April, 1992, was there any representative of the Serbian people in the presidency of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that they were there at the time, but Tatjana Ljujic-Mijatovic and Mirko Pejanovic, I believe, were members.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were they elected representatives of the Serbian people as members of the presidency, or did they function as a mere declaration in order to make the general public believe that the Serbian people were still represented at the presidency?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With Your Honours' indulgence, I should like to explain briefly the procedure concerning appointments to the presidency. The presidency itself has seven members. Each of the three peoples have their representatives there, but also other ethnic groups are represented with a member. The list of the Bosniaks, Bosniak representatives, had, for example, seven members. Then there was a list of Serb representatives, Serb candidates with seven to nine names. And another list of Croats with a similar number of candidates. And also, the fourth list representing the so-called "others" meaning other ethnic groups, which also comprised six to seven representatives. And finally, those who gained the majority of votes were elected representatives to the presidency. Should any of -- if any of the candidates thus elected ceases to be a member of the presidency, either on his or her own will or due to reasons of illness or death, his place is taken up by the candidate who was next in order on the list of candidates. Therefore, through this legal procedure, Mr. Mirko Pejanovic, a very respected and eminent academic was elected as a representative of the Serb people. And also elected with him was Tatjana Mijatovic-Ljujic also an academic, a university professor. Highly qualified people, very prominent and honourable individuals who would never allow themselves to be a mere decoration in the presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If that was indeed the procedure that was applied at the time, why was not Fikret Abdic elected as a member of the presidency, since he was the person who had received the majority of votes of the Bosniak people?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your statement is not correct. Fikret Abdic did serve as a member of the presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why wasn't he the president of the presidency, given the fact that he had received the majority of votes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please don't overlap.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In accordance with the law of Bosnia and Herzegovina, members of the presidency are elected through the elections. At the first constituent session of the presidency, the members, the elected members of the presidency, elect the president. So it was the members of the presidency who elected, as the president of the presidency, Mr. Alija Izetbegovic and not Fikret Abdic. His appointment was the reflection of their will.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As a representative of other ethnic groups, was Mr. Ejup Ganic a member of the presidency, in that capacity?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thereafter, did he become a prominent member of the Party of Democratic Action?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me go back to the attacks on the military convoys. Or as you said, conflicts with the military columns in Tuzla and Dobravojacka Street in Sarajevo. Do you know how many soldiers were killed in these columns?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of an attack of a military convoy which was supposed to pass through Kozarac two days after the incident in Hambarine?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did hear about it, but I do not have any precise information. According to what I know, what was already Serbian Army and not the JNA, officially speaking, issued, first of all, an ultimatum and then proceeded with attacking the checkpoints manned by the Territorial Defence in Kozarac. That was the way it happened, so your statement is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What did this ultimatum concern, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The contents of the ultimatum were pronounced by Radmilo Zeljaja on the 16th of May, 1992. During the negotiations which were supposed to be held between the representatives of the SDA and the SDS. I will try to paraphrase. "There can be no negotiations. There's no more Yugoslav People's Army. From today on, we are Serbian Army, and all members of the Territorial Defence and the reserve police force are hereby requested to turn in all of their weapons. All citizens of Bosniak ethnicity shall Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. declare their loyalty to the Serbian Republic and shall respond to the mobilisation into the Serbian army. If you try to make any move, do bear in mind that we have the weapons, including guns, Howitzers, helicopters, tanks, and missile systems and that any attempt on your part to put up a resistance will be severely punished."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Your Honours, I would like now to introduce one document we received recently from the OTP. It has been translated. So I would like the usher to distribute the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, we did check, the last document, S6B -- excuse me, D6, there is a translation available, and we can distribute that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this. And do I understand that you don't have any objections for the admission into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Of D6, I have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then for the record, the document tendered before by the Defence is admitted into evidence as D6B in B/C/S and D6A in English. Question to the Defence: Does this document have a 65 ter number?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: It does not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. Then I understand that the first part is the English translation of the handwritten second part. Right?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. You are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. And if I can just explain, this does not have ERN number. I could be corrected if I'm wrong, but my understanding if these are the documents that were received in the last few days, these were Defence exhibits on the Tadic appeal. So that's the only information we have about them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then for the record, this should go as D7A and D7B. And apologising in advance if we would have, but if not, the Bench would like also to have this document available to be prepared in future. Because the documents evidently provided by the OTP to the Defence, I'm not aware that they are available also for the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have provided the Defence probably 50.000 pages, or 20.000 pages in this case. This is not anything --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Of course, we are -- you know we have 20 binders disclosed until the beginning of the case. But whenever you regard it as necessary to give new documents to the Defence, then also the Bench should be aware of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are under continuing obligation under Rule 68 to give the Defence documents. We have provided thousands of pages, much more than 20 binders. The 20 binders is just the 65 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just to Your Honours' information. We do not know what documents the Defence proposes to use. Our position is it's only fair if the Defence out of the thousands and thousands of pages we have proposes to have a witness we notify us and the Bench so that copies are provided to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This, indeed, would be of great assistance for our work. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Dr. Mujadzic, let me start with asking you if you have ever seen this document?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is the first time I'm looking at this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you recognise the handwriting?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The document that you have in front of you, does it have the date the 30th of April, 1992, in the upper corner of the B/C/S version?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you be so kind and turn to the next page which bears the date the 2nd of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] [In English]... the page in English, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Under Item 1, can you please read out what it says. That sentence and the one after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry that I interrupt, but it's for the Bench also to understand the context. Could anybody please explain what are the minutes of what? Because we don't have any cover sheet at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] We really don't have any date on this, Your Honour. Maybe my learned friend can explain. We just received it as a 68.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: The only information I have is that these documents were submitted as part of the Tadic appeal. I believe they purport to be minutes of the meeting of a Crisis Staff or Territorial Defence, I'm not sure which, from Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If Your Honours allow, we may go through the document, and later on we could try to provide you with more information. So maybe it should only be provisional.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Let us proceed this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just to be clear, my understanding is these were never seized by the OTP. So we can't provide information on the source.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll try our best to show the relevance. If not, being provisional, it can be rejected at a later date.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dr. Mujadzic, if you're unable to read this handwriting --

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can follow the English version, if you want. I fully understand the English text, whereas I have some difficulty with reading this handwriting. Some of the parts are not fully legible, and the copy is not always very good.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you want me to read the document, and then you can confirm what I read, or would you prefer to read it yourself?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's up to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Since we are looking at the English version, we won't be needing the B/C/S version for the time being. I am interested in the text which follows this second date, the 2nd of May, 1992. Can you just read out what is written at the bottom of this page, page 1. The bottom of page 1.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the 30th of April or the 2nd of May?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The 2nd of May.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see, in the English version, the date the 2nd of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's at the bottom of the first page.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're quite right, yes. I can see it now. [In English] "2nd May, 1992. First, the security situation in the Kozarac area, total mobilisation of the STO, Territorial Defence staff report from the area." There is no --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether the personnel of the Territorial Defence in Kozarac was ever mobilised after the 2nd of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a public callup of the presidency of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina to carry it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Will you please turn to page 2 of the English text. We have Item Number 2, Item Number 3, and then under number 1 again, we read the name Nagib. It is a name, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Will you please read out the first sentence which is here recorded as the statement given by this man.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "A lot of our people carry out acts of provocation. Faslic and Hasan Didin yesterday fired in order to provoke. The police should immediately take such people to the police station and disarm them."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your opinion, does this show that there was shooting even without any orders being issued? It is obvious someone fired and an order was given to the police to arrest them.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It doesn't say here that the members of the Serb army were fired at. But there is an order for any such people to be arrested. But if only I may be allowed to read out a very brief sentence, a sentence by Becir Medunjanin, who was the secretary of national Defence: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. [In English] "Prijedor can't help us at all, state of readiness of the entire population, not to undertake actions with the aim of provoking, this is the scenario Miskovic outlined in Kozarski Vjesnik, the party and the municipality should be contacted, the main road issue."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does this show, as you have said, that Serbs had taken over the town and that the surrounding area was still under the control of the Territorial Defence, speaking in terms of the Bosniak population?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct. And it goes to confirm what I have said. Everyone was convinced that they could not resist, and that therefore, they should not carry out any acts of provocation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you be so kind as to go back to page 2 and find on the left-hand side the name Kenjar S. Can you read the statement here?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] "Civic disobedience should also be discussed with other areas. In Kozarac, some guys are provoking too much."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But there are no indications here that the army or the JNA carried out any such acts of provocation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you now be so kind as to go to the very end of this four-page document. You have the numbers marked at the bottom of the page. Let's go back to the next document, please, page 1.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean translation 323?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes, that's right. [Interpretation] Can you locate the name Medunjanin? It is underlined on this page.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you just read out this one single line, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] "I propose, if Cirkin agrees, that he should take over the RKS local Crisis Staff."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was Mr. Cirkin the head of the local Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to my information, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mind if I read this again?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is an opinion by some members. [In English] "The staff --" [Interpretation] It's the same page that we looked at just a while ago, the name Fazlic. Second sentence. [In English] The staff must be refreshed with new people, even different nationalities, and people shouldn't be late for meetings in the future. [Interpretation] Therefore, this staff did not have the intention of attacking anyone, but it wanted to involve other ethnic groups, too. The transcript also shows in a different statement that there were a number of members who proposed that Serb citizens should also join the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you be so kind now, please, as to go to the page 321 of this document, and under number 2, we see the name "Osman" underlined. Have you found this?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please read the passage out to us.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] "Osman: The present situation is entirely the result of the creation of a Serbian municipality. No policeman has signed, and a meeting with them, where they are to say if they wish to remain loyal has been scheduled for Friday. They are being asked to wear Serbian insignia or return the weapons. I propose: That the MZ," [Interpretation] local commune, [In English] "link up with another MZ at the level of the Prijedor municipality, and that an association of municipalities be formed, which would include Kozarac, Ljubija, and Grad, and where the laws of the Republic of B and H would be in force. This should be an interim solution, pending a lasting solution at B and H level. If the authorities are not recognised, they have to be told that."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does this represent an attempt to establish a municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The situation was quite chaotic. People were trying to organise themselves. I prefer to say that it was an attempt to organise the part that was free. There is not a word here about the establishment of a municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you now please go to page 312. It's the last page of the English document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry, until now, the Bench has shown a lot of tolerance, but it would be unfair to proceed without at least touching upon page 320, because this enlightens what we are discussing. If the witness could be so kind and read the top of this page of 6 June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [In English] "Meeting of Kozarac and Kozarusa Local Communes. Agenda: General and political security situation in the Prijedor municipality with particular stress on the situation in Kozarac and Kozarusa local communes. Miscellaneous."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Just for clarification, meeting of communes, what does it mean? Which board or which representative of the communes are meeting here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Prijedor comprised 70 local communes. These are small units, communities that the municipality was made up of. The meeting we are talking about is a meeting between two of these 70 small units that make up the whole.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Does this have anything to do with a kind of Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I can tell, this was a meeting of local communes. Therefore, any citizens could have been present at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for these enlightening words. Then, of course, the Defence may proceed with the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First of all, thanks to the Trial Chamber for their assistance. And I would like to please ask you to go back to page 312. We find the name Bahonjic on that page, and a remark made by that person. Could you please be so kind as to read it out.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] "If the people from Kozarac want to surrender the weapons, let them so. The people from Jakupovici will kill a few Serbs, so let Kozarac" -- the end of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So first of all, was the possibility of turning in the weapons discussed in Kozarac at all?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. As far as I know, it was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was this before or after the clash? I mean, when were the weapons turned in, before or after the clash?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure. I think part of it was surrendered before the clash, but I can't say with any degree of certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was there a checkpoint in Jakupovici?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Several days later following the clash in Kozarac, was there an attack on Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is also information I obtained from other people, secondhand information, and I'm not sure whether I can present any chronological sequence of these events.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You talked about a possible defence plan for the left river bank of the Sana River. Did you cross to the left bank, to Hambarine, in order to organise this defence?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. It was for security reasons that I crossed the river, as I have already mentioned before. Being a physician, I have no talents or specialist knowledge necessary to organise something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your conversation with Mr. Fikret Kadiric, did you try to convince him to assume the role of someone who would organise the police and the overall defence? Did you say that you were a deputy, and at that moment representing the state by virtue of being a deputy in that particular place?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that I asked Mr. Kadiric in his position as the head of police to get himself involved in an attempt to organise any sort of civilian authority and to get people organised. But the latter allegation is not true. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you please like to tell us what exactly isn't true?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The allegation that I had said that I was authority in that area, that I was representing the authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know what Kadiric answered?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see you seem to assume that I asked him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have no idea what he stated. Can you help us, please, and tell us?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kadiric said: "Mirza, I would love to do it, but I am not allowed to do it. I have two daughters. If I do anything, they will kill them and rape them."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you make any threats to Mr. Kadiric that he will have to account for not accepting this offer for a position?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no threats. After I received the reply from him that I have just quoted, our conversation was interrupted, and I said: "Yes, I can fully understand this. I can fully understand your position." If I may just add, related to your question addressed to Your Honours related to your suggestion yesterday that we had organised some sort of war staff, no such war staff was ever organised, nor did any such staff ever operate. And its name was not "war staff." The idea that I did have was to establish a legal council, a national defence council, because with its president, Muhamed Cehajic, in addition to him, there were other four legally appointed members, the head of police, national defence secretariat commander of civilian protection Enes Kusavic [phoen], and I think also the MPs club president would also be appointed. This National Defence Council had to be added to. This idea was never really implemented. Further members should have been republican MPs, and this was envisaged as a body to organise some sort of interim government. So under the law of Bosnia and Herzegovina, such a body would have had full legality and legitimacy. Yesterday, the whole time you tried to invert this by trying to show the National Defence Council, led by Mr. Cehajic, and its functioning by trying to replace the National Defence Council, to confuse it with the Crisis Staff presided by Milomir Stakic. The National Defence Council did operate under the laws of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and its president could not issue orders, did not have authority to issue orders to the head of police or the chief of civilian protection. The Crisis Staff led by Mr. Stakic was half military in its character, whereby Mr. Stakic did have the authority to both order and exercise command and could influence the police and the Territorial Defence. I apologise, but I felt that I had to present this brief explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar the members of the Territorial Defence and the Patriotic League, did they plan to attack the barracks in Bihac and to take -- to seize the weapons that were in the barracks?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure about the existence of any such plans. I don't think there were any such plans, to the best of my knowledge. In Bihac, negotiations were held with a general whose name I can't remember right now, a general from the Bihac Corps. He safely left Bihac with all his army and all his weapons. Immediately following that event, the Belgrade media, the Serbian media, he appeared there, and he boastfully spoke about how he successfully cheated the Bosniaks out of all the weapons and safely escaped with his army. And these were really were facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you make any efforts that -- to the effect that the people who had received weapons from the Territorial Defence surrender these weapons to people that you would have appointed, people who were more favoured by the SDA and people who were more along the lines of SDA policies?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. My efforts were for the Territorial Defence, which was in an area that was later not occupied by the Serb army, for the Territorial Defence to be unified in its activity and to be coordinated. These were my efforts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just one last question before the break, did you make any efforts to the effect that the people who had been given weapons by the Territorial Defence pass these weapons on to someone else?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I've already answered this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So your testimony is that you did not make any such efforts?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] It would be an appropriate time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Before we take the break, in order to save time, I have some problems with the documents presented under D7B. As far as I can follow, and the Bench can follow the text in B/C/S, there are some portions in addition in English which we can't find in B/C/S. And especially, we can't identify in the English version, on page 312, the portion on a person Bahonjic. The Defence asked the witness to read out, and I can't see it in B/C/S. Probably during the break, both the witness and the Defence can assist us. Thank you. And then we stay adjourned until 11.00 sharp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have a document which I recently got from my investigators, and it hasn't been translated also. It's a document from -- actually, a clip from the newspapers, and it's an interview of Dr. Mujadzic given to one Bosnian newspaper. So I would like this to be distributed, and I have some questions regarding this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. Can we in the meantime, in order not to be confused, to come back briefly to Document D7. Could you identify that what you read out in English in the B/C/S part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could you please give us the page number.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's page 338 in the B/C/S version, at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [In English] Yes, 338.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Our document concludes with 328.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The B/C/S version, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: 338, yes. And there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the bottom of the page, we can indeed read the sentence in question. However, there is no -- the end of the discussion, or rather the end of the intervention by Mr. Bahonjic is missing. But judging from other interventions, and I can give Your Honour an example by the same speaker, the same person, I don't think that the intention was to kill Serbs. There was just a talk about the danger, the risk that that might happen. This was taken out of the context of the overall discussion. As an argument to support this, we can have a look at the page 333 of the B/C/S version. Let me read it out to you. This is the -- an intervention of the same speaker, on a later date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can we get the date, and then we can perhaps find it in the English. Because the page numbers seem to me to be nonsensical as far as the order between both the English and the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In the B/C/S, it's the 6th of May, 1992. And you want to guide us to 333. And then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 333 in the B/C/S version. I'm not sure that it corresponds to the English translation. There is a lot of confusion with the pages of both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I believe the witness may be speaking about page 315, the May 8th meeting where Mr. Bahonjic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think if you read the B/C/S, we can compare.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, that is not the issue. Unfortunately, Bahonjic is saying the following: "The preservation of peace was essential, and the need to buy some time. In order for us to be able to oppose this might with intelligence, we should all go out into the field and try and explain this to the people. We are talking about -- we are discussing with the force which is not afraid of anything. If there Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. should be an implementation of the law of Bosnia and Herzegovina, then we will be faced with an unwanted evil." So it is clear that the same person, the same speaker, is recommending the preservation of peace, that we should all try and to negotiate. No other option is being proposed here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: That which you just quoted we can find in English on page 315, the third paragraph. But thank you for your clarification on this. And I apologise for interrupting the Defence. Are there any objections against the admission of this bundle of documents we have now under D7A and D7B?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: At this time, I will not, in any way, wish to indicate that we believe these are legitimate. There is a witness who will testify in a few weeks who is quoted in these documents, and he may be able to verify these are legitimate minutes. I have no reason to doubt that they are, but I don't know their source at all. But Mr. Sejmenovic who is not protected is quoted, and he may be able to tell us if these are legitimate minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But following our policy, when in doubt, to admit into he have that what is tendered by the parties. Thereby, this bundle of documents is admitted into evidence under D7A and D7B. May we now turn to the D8, and the floor is for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dr. Mujadzic, did you ever give an interview to Refik Hodzic, on the basis of which this article entitled "Mirza Mujadzic, Traitor or a Hero" was published?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was this article published in Novo Ogledalo magazine?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you be so kind and read out to the Chamber, since we do not have the translation of this document at this point, starting from -- with the second column of the text of the interview, which is entitled "the defence line along the Sana River." And if you will please read out the text which is highlighted in green. There is a small portion between these highlighted portions which you can also read so that we know what the connection between the two is.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the outset, I have to draw your attention to the fact that this was a series of articles which were published in the Novo Ogledalo magazine. However, I never had the authority to authorise this text, although I had asked the journalist, Mr. Refik Hodzic to allow me to authorise the article. But he never complied with this request, so this cannot be interpreted as an authentic statement of mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But nevertheless, I can read out, and then probably comment on this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "In early April 1992, the Bihac municipal staff of the Territorial Defence, of course, its Bosnian segment, was supposed to carry out an attack on the Bihac barracks to recover all the weapons there and to make sure that, in the course of the month of May, all the forces are pushed to the left bank of the Sana River, according to the plan." Is that what you wanted to hear?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you please continue.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well. "The republic staff of the Patriotic League actually concluded that the only area that could be defended was the left bank of the Sana River and that the territories on the right bank of the river, at least in the initial stage of the attack, could simply not be defended. This implied an evacuation of all combat troops from the right bank of the Sana to the left bank, and also, on the other hand, the transfer of all military units from Cazin and Kladusa to the left bank. This is supposed to constitute the defence line, which corresponded with the geographical line of the Sana and also the rear part of the left bank. That area being a large Muslim/Croatian area."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The same idea is explained further in the text. Did you actually state this to the journalist in question?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said something to this effect in my previous testimony, although not perhaps using the same words. If you remember, I had mentioned the idea in Bihac that the left bank of the Sana River should be defended. If you remember, I indicated on the map that this excluded the urban area of Sanski Most, Prijedor, and Kljuc, and that the idea concerned only certain territories on the left bank of the Sana. So I already testified about this before the Court. I told you that this idea of defence existed at one point in time in the area of Bihac. But I believe that I also said that once Krupa had fallen on the 23rd of April, this idea became absurd and that we found ourselves completely cut off.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As regards the attack on the Bihac barracks, is there anything that you can tell us about it? Is that what you stated?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is -- these were not my exact words. You know as well as I do that journalists sometimes interpret the original text on their own, and I emphasise that I did not authorise this text. These are not my actual words.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does this apply only to this particular paper, or is it your standing objection to all magazines and newspapers in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did give a number of interviews. Some of them were authorised by me, but I think that the majority of such texts were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm not referring to your statements; I am referring to a general practice by journalists who are sometimes want to interpret and paint the situation the way they want to present it.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That really depends on the paper in question. And of course, the reputation of the paper depends on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you please turn to the next page and focus on the column in the middle. There is a title at the bottom of the column "50 people in Prijedor PL" and there is a question preceding it. Can you read the highlighted part, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the middle column? Middle paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What exactly do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Will you start please with the question and then go on until the end of the section highlighted in green.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see any question here. I don't see a question in the middle column.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is a title which says "50 people in Prijedor PL." This is the middle column. That is the only subtitle on this page.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes, I see. You said the section highlighted in green. That's why I wasn't clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's probably a mistake. Will you start with the question: "What happened with the Patriotic League?"

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where do you see this? Oh, yes, I see. "What happened with the Patriotic League."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Will you please read out the paragraph that follows, and then the highlighted one which is at the top of the next column.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We have some difficulties because indeed, what we can identify as your passage you want to be read out is not highlighted in green at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since there seems to be a confusion here, Your Honour, would you accept me reading the text, and then we can hear the comment by Dr. Mujadzic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, please. We start with the question: "A sta je bilo sa Patriotskom Ligom?"

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] That's right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "And what happened with the Patriotic League? 50 people in the Prijedor Patriotic League. Mujadzic quote: "When we tried to cooperate, after the mobilisation had been carried out, we decided that those people who were with the local staffs of the Territorial Defence and who, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. therefore, had uniforms, logistics, weapons, ammunition, everything, and who were supposed to constitute a corps on the basis of which the remainder of the military-age men had to be mobilised in each of the local communes, that that should be carried out and unified. We established that the structure in question was actually a very carefully selected structure by the former JNA, that it consisted of people who had been carefully selected, and that it was not possible to communicate or cooperate with them in any meaningful way. The only exception to this was Kozarac. Kozarac was well organised indeed, and connected with the Territorial Defence staff. They even had their own command at the level of the entire Kozarac, and a system which was very well connected." Dr. Mujadzic, my question to you, were you dissatisfied with the people who had the weapons that had been distributed by the Territorial Defence, and did you try to secure the transfer of these weapons to some other people, as I have already asked you?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, and I don't think this is how you can interpret these words as well. My statement was that these people had been carefully hand-picked by the JNA, and therefore, that it was impossible to cooperate with them. I didn't say that I was trying to force someone to do something. And I also believe that I already explained this in my testimony, either on Monday or on Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then you go on and speak about the Patriotic League, which is indicated in the heading of this column. In this passage, you say the following: "At the same time, we were carrying out a political propaganda with the objective of having these people accepted by the population, so that the weapons should be handed over to them and so that from that corps, one day we could have a bigger, a larger formation, larger unit. In order to have such corps of people established in every local commune, which units would be then linked up with other units in the overall system." Were you talking about your requests that the weapons be handed over to the members of the Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, let me stress that this is not an authentic text. It does not exactly correspond to what I had stated. And I reiterate, we said that those people who were not intending to use their weapons, and there were many such people, so I was -- I'm referring to the 1.700 pieces of legally possessed weapons, either personal weapons or hunting weapons, and also in view of the decision of the presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina to carry out a mobilisation of the people with the objective of replenishing Territorial Defence units. And this is what we were doing. We were implementing the decision of the presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina. This text does not indicate that I or anybody else forced anyone to hand over their weapons to the Patriotic League.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I did not exactly use the word "force." I said whether you carried out propaganda for the weapons to be handed over to other persons, other Bosniak persons. I apologise in case you have misunderstood my words.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's all right. Apology accepted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that, at the police centre in Hrasnica, a secret meeting was held on the 10th of June, 1991, at which the national defence association was established, the National Defence Council that you referred to just before the break?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing was said about any national defence association, so you must have misinterpreted something that I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Perhaps that's because I'm tired. I seem to be misinterpreting quite a number of things today. Do you know anything about the establishment of this National Defence Council on the 10th of June, 1991?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember any such meeting, or at least I did not attend any such meeting. And I had no information on any such meeting being held in Hrasnica at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were the details of the defence of the left bank of the River Sana familiar to the general staff of the BH army, in terms of an order by the general staff with description of the precise movements and maneuvers to be carried out by the units?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This question can't be answered by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you please be so kind as to turn to the next page of your interview, the second page of your interview.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Marked as page 6, or 46?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The top of the first passage, line 5, you state the following: "This is only a global view of this plan. But the details were available at the general staff (Of the BH army -- journalist's note) in the form of an order by the general staff containing the precise manoeuvres to be carried out by units."

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This must have been added by the journalist on the basis of information that he may have had. This is not a statement I made. That is, I was never familiar with any such document simply because I was not in a position to know, as I was not involved with military issues. I was not part of any military staff and therefore was not in a position to be informed about anything like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that on the 7th and 8th of February, there was the final agreement on the plan for the defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and on the 25th of February, 1992, in Hrasnica, the main staff of the Patriotic League passed a directive to defend the sovereignty of Bosnia and Herzegovina? Are you familiar with any of these?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Politically speaking, yes, I was informed, as I have already said in my testimony, about the fact that the area containing the town of Prijedor and the majority of the Banja Luka area, the greatest part of the Banja Luka area, could not be defended, and I said this. Concerning any details of the decisions by the general staff or the army, I really can't tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you now please turn to page 46. Third column, third passage, beginning with the word "the second." I will read out the part beginning with line 5 of this passage. This is a statement ascribed to you, and it begins towards the end of the second passage. "First I tried to convince Kadiric, who was the police commander, to take over the role of organising the police and the overall defence. He was an experienced man, and he was well respected in the Brdo area. He categorically refused to be involved in this. Finally, I told him, Listen, we have at present no connection with Sarajevo. We have no connection with the state level. But I am here. I am a deputy to the republican assembly. At this moment, I represent the state, in a way, in this area. If there is ever the rule of law in this state, you will be made to account for this. You must know that I will point you out as the responsible one because you are not doing your duty, the duty you're supposed to be doing." Was this also a misquote?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you can just read the sentence to the end, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "You must put together all the policemen, and even further, you must organise here in this place, if nothing else, at least for law and order to be observed."

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that I called upon Kadiric to do his duty as police commander, to ensure that law and order were observed. But as the presidency had already issued an order for the Territorial Defence to be organised and mobilised, so this was an order carrying full legality and legitimacy, and knowing that the police forces were part of the armed forces in any state, it is true that I requested him to do this. But what is not true is that I myself said that I was representing the state in this area. This is also an interpretation by the journalist. I would like to point out to Your Honours that the journalist, or the whole group of people that I released this interview to, were people obviously who were not sympathetic to my cause. And it was because I had doubted the authenticity of their article, I requested authorisation before Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. publishing, but they denied me this possibility and they published the series of articles without my authorisation. So what you have read out right now, I have already explained.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know Asim Music, Kemal Alagic, also known as Divljak, Slavko Ecimovic, Major Mirsad Selimbegovic, and Mr. Sead Cirkin?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know all these people, but I met them after the war. That is, some of them I had not known before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were these people in charge of organising military issues in Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can we just go through their names again to the sake of precision? I think you mentioned another name, Asim Muhic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Let me just ask the witness whether there's any reason for us to do this in private session. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You shouldn't apologise. You agree that it's in private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And I propose that those names be redacted interest the transcript from the open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: If they are named in the article, I don't think there's a necessity to redact.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: These names are not in the article.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Both of them, I could see myself --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Not all of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So let's only redact those names which are not in the article. Can we go through? It was on line -- we are in private session now, that we don't make another mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Confirmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like now to tender another document received from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we agree, first of all, that the article you tendered until now, this would go as D8B, and it's only tendered to that extent that it was read out and we have the translation in the transcript. Right?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I object. I'd like to point out something regarding that procedure. I don't know, because I don't have a translation, whether the quotes are out of context or whether there are other parts of the article that are relevant. And I don't want to make a -- I'm not accusing counsel of anything, but the Defence can submit this to CLSS for translation, which is part of the registry, not part of the OTP. And I would suggest that any article that's going to be admitted into evidence should be submitted for full translation so that we can find out whether the quotes are in context or out of context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Until now, we followed the policy also as regards the documents tendered by the OTP to admit only the relevant sections into evidence. And therefore, it is for the OTP, if there is any problem, to come back to this with an entire translation. But until now, let's proceed this way. And therefore, this document is admitted into evidence as D8B. On page 44, in the middle column, the eight last lines, and in the right-hand column, until the 11th last line. On page 45, the left hand column, line 5 to 9; middle column, the 13 last lines; and the right hand column until last line 11 in the middle. And page 46, lines in the right hand column, line 23 to 41. And the translations can be found on today's transcript, page 32. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would like to tender another document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Do we have any 65 ter number?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I don't think that there is a 65 ter, and there is no ERN number either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We also received this document recently from the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: It's the same situation, I believe, from the Tadic appeal submitted by the Defence on that appeal.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So I'll try to read portions and ask Dr. Mujadzic to comment on those portions I read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: For the record, provisionally D9A and B.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's also handwritten, so I would prefer to read the English version, if you allow it, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mujadzic, these are the minutes. And at the top of the first page, we see what this is about. It says: "Minutes, 24th of October, 1991. At the SDA Party of Democratic Action meeting, the following were assigned to weapons duty: Kozarac: Kenjar, Bahonjic; Trnopolje: Sead Sivac; Kozarusa: Tadic; Brdo and Ljubija: Kadiric, Hopovac, Sikiric; Puharska, Rufad Suljanovic." [Interpretation] Can you please help us out with this. What exactly did this mean, when on the 24th of October, 1991, a number of persons were appointed to take charge of certain activities associated with weapons?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC [Resumed]
